facts.statement: The only known species, Elmisaurus rarus, lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Elmisaurus rarus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Elmisaurus (mon. "lagarto pie") de dinosaurio terópodo cenagnátido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Two fragmentary specimens of a small theropod were discovered in 1970 by a Polish-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovĭ province of Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1970, a paleontological Polish-Mongolian expedition discovered two fragmentary specimens of a small theropod in the Ömnögovĭ province of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The generic name means "foot sole" because the type specimen consisted of a metatarsus.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Mongol or , "foot sole", as the type specimen consisted of a metatarsus.

facts.statement: Elmisaurus rarus was discovered in 1970 and described in 1981 by Halszka Osmólska.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1970 y descrito en 1981, por Halszka Osmólska.

facts.statement: Due to the fragmentary nature of the fossils, the appearance is uncertain, but the holotype body length is estimated at 1.68 meters.
facts.quote: Dada la naturaleza fragmentaria de los hallazgos, la apariencia de Elmisaurus rarus es muy incierta. La longitud del cuerpo del holotipo se estima en 1,68 metros.

facts.statement: Like all oviraptorosaurs, Elmisaurus was a feathered, warm-blooded biped.
facts.quote: Al igual que con todos los oviraptorosaurios, este es un bípedo emplumado, de sangre caliente.

facts.statement: The foot was light and slender, measuring about 15 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El pie es ligero y delgado, de unos 15 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The hand was about 20 centimeters long and slender, with bone shafts much narrower than the ends, a feature not found in other oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: La mano tiene una longitud de unos 20 centímetros y es otra vez delgada, especialmente con los vástagos de los huesos mucho más estrechos que los extremos, una característica que no se encuentra en otros oviraptorosaurios.

facts.statement: The hand claws were strongly curved.
facts.quote: Las garras de las manos están fuertemente curvadas.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests the forehead bones showed a high crest continuing through the nose.
facts.quote: Los huesos de la frente parecen mostrar una alta cresta que continúa a través de la nariz.

facts.statement: The vertebrae were highly pneumatized.
facts.quote: Las vértebras están muy neumatizadas.

facts.statement: The shoulder joint directed outward and downward.
facts.quote: La articulación del hombro se dirige hacia afuera y hacia abajo.

facts.statement: The first finger was slender.
facts.quote: El primer dedo es delgado.

facts.statement: A bump on the top surface of the fourth metatarsal protruded over the fifth metatarsal bone and rose above the midfoot joint surface.
facts.quote: Un bulto en la superficie superior del cuarto metatarsiano sobresale del quinto hueso metatarsiano y se eleva sobre la superficie articular del mediopié.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined 23 foot bones referred to Elmisaurus for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 23 foot bones referred to Elmisaurus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: Elmisaurus rarus is the first discovered caenagnathid for which hands and feet are known.
facts.quote: Elmisaurus rarus es el primer cenagnátido descubierto que se conocen las manos y pies.

facts.statement: In 1997, Hans-Dieter Sues argued that the second species should be referred to Chirostenotes, a view not accepted by Philip J. Currie.
facts.quote: In 1997, Hans-Dieter Sues stated that this supposed second species of Elmisaurus should be referred to Chirostenotes, as C. elegans, though this position was not accepted by Currie.

facts.statement: Elmisaurus was previously considered a relative of Chirostenotes within Elmisauridae and later Caenagnathidae, but this relationship was questioned by Maryanska et al. in 2002.
facts.quote: Elmisaurus se ha visto como pariente de Chirostenotes, primero en Elmisauridae y más adelante en Caenagnathidae, hasta los descubrimientos recientes, cuando esto fue cuestionado por Maryanska et al. en 2002.

facts.statement: While a relationship with Avimimus is possible, a 2007 analysis by Senter places Elmisaurus with Chirostenotes and Hagryphus, far from Avimimus.
facts.quote: La relación con Avimimus es posible, pero el análisis de Senter en 2007 coloca a Elmisaurus con Chirostenotes y Hagryphus, lejos de Avimimus.

facts.statement: A 2013 analysis by Longrich et al. classified Elmisaurus as a caenagnathid.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows an analysis by Longrich et al. in 2013, which found Elmisaurus to be a caenagnathid.

facts.statement: A 2007 analysis by Senter places Elmisaurus with Chirostenotes and Hagryphus, distinct from Avimimus.
facts.quote: El análisis de Senter en 2007 coloca a Elmisaurus con Chirostenotes y Hagryphus, lejos de Avimimus.

facts.statement: Elmisaurus lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The paratype specimen ZPAL MgD-I/20 is one-fifth longer than the holotype.
facts.quote: ZPAL MgD-I/20 es un quinto más largo.
